# ADR: Evaluate AI SDLC / SpecKit Tooling (Issue #3115)

## Comparison Matrix

| Tool | Category | Primary problem solved | Best use case | S-CORE fit | Strengths | Weaknesses | Use / Do not use | Best partner tools |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **APM** | Packaging | Reproducible, governed distribution of agent context | Org-wide skill/MCP-server rollout to all contributors regardless of IDE | High | Policy engine, lockfile integrity, SBOM, broadest agent coverage (8) | Newest governance features unproven at scale; MS stewardship | **USE** | Pharaoh methodology, Spec Kit, `mcp-servers`, `sbom-tool` |
| **Lola** | Packaging | Same, lighter-weight | Small-team or pilot skill sharing | Medium | Simpler, vendor-neutral, OpenSSF badge | No lockfile hashes, no policy/SBOM, narrower agent coverage | **WATCH** (fallback only) | same as APM's list |
| **OKIT** | Packaging | Minimal skill copying | Personal prototyping only | Low | Zero dependencies, auditable | No versioning/security/marketplace, bus factor 1 | **DO NOT USE** | none at this maturity |

## Recommendations

### Packaging Layer
- **Primary:** APM (policy engine, lockfile integrity, SBOM export, broadest coverage)
- **Fallback:** Lola (simpler, vendor-neutral)
- **Not recommended:** OKIT (pre-production, bus factor 1)

## Next Steps

1. Execute proof-of-concept pilots for recommended primary tools
2. Validate integration with existing S-CORE infrastructure (Bazel, Sphinx, sphinx-needs)
3. Measure governance and audit outcomes
4. Update this ADR with results from pilot deployments
